CHIEF COMPLAINT
Postoperative follow-up after bilateral reduction mammoplasty.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 36-year-old female presenting for postoperative evaluation following bilateral reduction mammoplasty performed on 10-10-2020. She reports that her breasts are healing well. She denies chills, fever, nausea, or vomiting. She reports no current back pain. Patient notes that during a prior visit with PA Ruth Sanchez in March, a lump was noted under the left breast, which she has not felt since then and attributes to scar tissue. She has been performing massages and using scar gel daily. She reports that some scars, particularly in one area, have widened slightly and have been bothering her. She has been applying scar gel to help with the appearance. Patient declines revision surgery at this time and agrees to follow up in six months to reassess the scars.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chills, fever, nausea, vomiting, or back pain. No hard spots, lumps, or bumps currently appreciated by patient.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Bilateral reduction mammoplasty on 10-10-2020.

MEDICATIONS
Mederma scar gel (patient-applied topically).

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Family doing well; no acute concerns noted.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports enjoying summertime. No other social history documented.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Breasts: Bilateral incisions well healed with no signs of infection or redness. Some widening of scars noted, particularly in one area. Palpation reveals no masses. Overall healing progressing well.

RESULTS
None documented.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Successful postoperative recovery from bilateral reduction mammoplasty. Well-healed incisions without infection. Some scar widening noted but stable. Patient to continue Mederma scar gel application twice daily and massage. Revision of scars deferred until at least one year postoperatively. Follow-up appointment scheduled in six months to reassess scars and take photographs for documentation. Patient agreeable to plan.
